The recent series of actions were all aimed at getting a concrete visual of the rendered scene so I can diagnose why the FPS is stuck at near‑zero. I added a `__snap` helper to the page, reloaded, captured a JPEG data URL, and verified that the base64 string is being generated correctly. I then tried to POST that data URL back to the dev server, but the server currently only serves static files; it doesn’t have an endpoint to accept the screenshot. Rather than keep hacking around with ad‑hoc fetches, I decided to make a proper development server that can handle a `/snap` POST request and write the JPEG to disk. I wrote `devserver.py` with a simple `Handler` class that decodes the data URL and saves `snap.jpg`. To make the Claude launch configuration use this script, I edited `.claude/launch.json` to replace the default `http.server` arguments with `devserver.py`. Then I started (or rather reused) the preview server with `preview_start` under the name “wildwood”, which gave me back the same server ID and port as before.

Now the server is running with the new handler, but I still have the old preview instance active. If I try to run another `preview_start` with a different configuration, it will just reuse the existing server again, because the preview system reuses the same server process for the same name. What I actually need is to restart the preview server so that the changes to `devserver.py` take effect. The only way to guarantee a clean reload is to stop the current preview server and then start it again. Stopping requires calling the `mcp__Claude_Preview__preview_stop` tool, which takes the server ID (or name) and shuts down the process. I don't have a direct tool call ready for that yet, so the next logical step is to look up the exact tool name and usage. The tool catalog can be queried with a `ToolSearch`. By searching for `"select:mcp__Claude_Preview__preview_stop"` I can retrieve the definition of the stop tool (including its parameters) and then invoke it to terminate the server before I restart it. This will ensure the new `devserver.py` is loaded and the `/snap` endpoint works, allowing me to finally save the screenshot to disk for inspection.

Therefore, the immediate next action is to perform a ToolSearch for the preview stop tool.
